$comment: The CLOSED set of installable modules this repository may publish, and the
facts each release is checked against. A package absent from this file
cannot be built or published by `release-module.yml` — the workflow resolves
its target here and fails closed, so adding a publishable module is a
reviewed diff rather than a dispatch-time string.
`dotmac-kernel` and `dotmac-ui` are deliberately NOT here: they have their
own workflows with their own inspection rules (a kernel wheel must ship
compiled CSS; a module must not). One workflow pretending to cover both
would have to weaken whichever check the other cannot satisfy.
kernel_floor is the EARLIEST kernel that can actually load and register
the module — the highest of everything the module needs, not one fixed
rule. Two things set it:
1. the release that allocated its schema in MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER; an
earlier kernel raises UnallocatedNamespaceError and the module cannot
register at all;
2. the release that added any kernel CAPABILITY the manifest consumes —
e.g. ADR-0023's `platform_tables`, added in a49; an earlier kernel
raises TypeError at import, before the allocation check is reached.
For most modules (1) is the answer and (2) does not apply. Where both
apply the higher wins, and tests/architecture/test_kernel_version_sync.py
keeps the two cases in separate, reasoned maps so neither is silent.
Either way registry verification can only pass once that kernel is
published.
Listed for the ERP-first ticket adoption programme (ADR-0017's
2026-08-13 ticketing amendment). Until this entry existed the module
was unpublishable, so no product could pin it and the dossier's
`first_cutover` was unreachable by construction.
kernel_floor is a56, NOT the a39 that allocated mod_tkt. A CAPABILITY has
raised this floor twice: `platform_tables` (dual-plane, ADR-0023), then
the logical prerequisite contract (ADR-0006 D1 amendment) its manifest
and migration root now use. An earlier kernel cannot import the
manifest, so the check never reaches the allocation. Floor is set by a
kernel capability rather than by its own namespace row.
`alembic` is in allowed_requires and is NOT a packaging slip:
`dotmac_ticketing.linking`'s per-plane link helpers emit DDL into a
CONSUMING product's migration, so Alembic is imported at runtime by
them rather than used as a dev tool. The other modules ship no such
helper and correctly forbid it.
mod_files is allocated in kernel a54, and that allocation is ALSO the
floor: ADR-0023's dual-plane platform_tables landed earlier, in a53, so
the module's own namespace row is the higher of the two requirements.
This is the ordinary case; dotmac-ticketing is the exception.
The bulk-import run ledger (ADR-0025). kernel_floor is a56: mod_imports
was allocated in a55, but the lineage now declares `requires` and calls
resolve_depends_on / require_prerequisites (ADR-0006 D1 amendment),
which a56 added — so a capability, not the allocation, sets it.
No alembic in allowed_requires: this module ships its own im lineage
but emits no DDL into a CONSUMING product's migration, so Alembic is a
packaging input rather than a runtime import.
The connector control plane (ADR-0024 §§ 6-7). Listed so the
independently deployed `dotmac_integrator` assembly can PIN it — until
this entry existed the module was unpublishable, and an assembly that
cannot pin a module cannot compose it.
kernel_floor is a58, its OWN ledger allocation, not a capability raise.
It consumes `platform_tables` (a53) and the logical prerequisite
contract (a56), but the floor is the highest of everything the module
needs and its allocation is the highest — so pinning the allocation
picks up the a57 catalog correction transitively rather than needing a
second rule. That correction exists BECAUSE of this module: it is the
first platform-plane-only one, and a platform-only schema was demanding
tenant-role USAGE it must never hold.
Both migrations are required wheel contents, deliberately. This
repository does not compose the module — `app/assembly.py` omits it and
`alembic.ini` carries no `ig` lineage, because the Starter is a target
application and composing it would create `mod_intg` in every starter
deployment. A wheel that shipped the manifest but dropped a migration
would therefore fail first in the Integrator's deployment, not here.
No `alembic` in allowed_requires: unlike dotmac-ticketing this module
ships no link helper that emits DDL into a consuming product's
migration, so Alembic is a dev tool here and importing it at runtime
would be a packaging slip.
`secret_refs.py` is a required wheel content because it is the ADR-0024 § 7
enforcement point — a wheel that shipped the models but dropped the refusal
would accept secret VALUES into an immutable config revision and never
complain. It was named `secrets.py` until the release wheel-content policy
correctly refused it; renamed rather than exempted.
Approval state on two declared planes (ADR-0026). Listed only now that
the live Postgres migration and catalog gate has passed in this
repository's integration job: absence from this file was the safety
mechanism while it had not, and ADR-0026 section 8 says the entry lands
with the proof rather than ahead of it.
kernel_floor is a59, its OWN ledger allocation. It consumes
platform_tables (a53) and the logical prerequisite contract (a56), but
the floor is the highest of everything the module needs and its
allocation is the highest - the ordinary case, like dotmac-integration
and unlike dotmac-ticketing.
The migration is a required wheel content. This repository does not
compose the module - `app/assembly.py` omits it and `alembic.ini`
carries no `ap` lineage - so a wheel that shipped the manifest but
dropped the lineage would fail first in an ADOPTER's deployment rather
than here.
No `alembic` in allowed_requires: the module ships no helper that emits
DDL into a consuming product's migration, so Alembic is a packaging
input rather than a runtime import. `dotmac-ticketing` remains the only
module permitted it.
